payload.task_text:
I am preparing for a faculty meeting where we need to review quiz performance across our Fall 2014 courses. I need you to pull quiz data from our learning management system for all courses offered in that semester and summarize the results.

Scope definition (important, follow exactly): our LMS hosts the same subjects across multiple semesters (Fall 2013, Spring 2013, Spring 2014, Fall 2014), and the semester is identified by the suffix in the course name. "Fall 2014 courses" means exactly the courses whose Canvas course name ends with "(Fall 2014)": Applied Analytics & Algorithms (Fall 2014), Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Fall 2014), Creative Computing & Culture (Fall 2014), Data-Driven Design (Fall 2014), Environmental Economics & Ethics (Fall 2014), Foundations of Finance (Fall 2014), and Global Governance & Geopolitics (Fall 2014). Do not include any course whose name ends with a different semester suffix, and do not select courses by date ranges or enrollment terms — match on the course-name suffix only. Among these seven courses, only the ones that actually have quizzes in the LMS should appear in the outputs (a course with no quizzes at all is omitted entirely).

For each of those Fall 2014 courses, gather the quiz titles, the number of student submissions per quiz, the average score, the minimum score, and the maximum score. Count every quiz submission recorded in Canvas for that quiz regardless of its submission date, and compute the average/minimum/maximum over the submission scores. Then create an Excel spreadsheet called Quiz_Performance.xlsx in the workspace. The spreadsheet should have a sheet named "Quiz Details" with columns Course, Quiz_Title, Submissions, Avg_Score, Min_Score, and Max_Score. The Course column must contain the full Canvas course name including the "(Fall 2014)" suffix, e.g. "Creative Computing & Culture (Fall 2014)". The Avg_Score, Min_Score, and Max_Score should be rounded to two decimal places. Sort the rows first by Course name alphabetically, then by Quiz_Title alphabetically within each course.

Also add a second sheet called "Course Summary" that aggregates at the course level over the same quiz-bearing Fall 2014 courses. It should have columns Course (again the full course name with the "(Fall 2014)" suffix), Total_Quizzes (number of quizzes in that course), Total_Submissions (sum across all quizzes), and Overall_Avg_Score which is the weighted average of quiz scores across all submissions for that course rounded to two decimal places, i.e. sum(avg_score * submissions) / sum(submissions) over the course's quizzes. Sort alphabetically by Course.

Finally, create a PowerPoint presentation called Quiz_Report.pptx in the workspace. The first slide should be a title slide with the title "Fall 2014 Quiz Performance Report" and subtitle "Faculty Meeting Summary". Then create one dedicated slide per quiz-bearing Fall 2014 course with the course name as the title and a text body listing the number of quizzes, total submissions, and overall average score for that course. Add a final slide with the title "Key Takeaways" and body text stating which course had the highest overall average score and which had the lowest.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, keep the large quiz-submission reads outside the main context with exactly one parallel collector wave, freeze the gathered statistics into a single JSON handoff file, and let the main agent itself build both deliverables — no planning sub-agent, no second wave.

The main agent first resolves the runtime workspace, calls canvas_list_courses(include_ended=true) once, and retains exactly the seven fixed Fall 2014 courses by full-name suffix "(Fall 2014)" (never by date range or enrollment term). Then, natively in parallel, it calls canvas_list_quizzes once per retained course and records each course's literal quiz_ids. A course with zero quizzes is omitted from all outputs. Before dispatch, freeze one assignment manifest entry per quiz-bearing course: course_id|course_name|quiz_ids.

Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 3 explore sub-agents in parallel, one per quiz-bearing Fall 2014 course below. Omit zero-quiz courses from this wave.

   1. explore 0 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): Collector for course_id=7 "Creative Computing & Culture (Fall 2014)": fetch the full quiz-submission records for every quiz in its course (canvas quiz-submission listing, per_page=100, follow pagination.has_page/pagination.has_more, and always read the FULL JSON from the output_path file when the chat preview is truncated); count every recorded submission regardless of date; compute per quiz Submissions (count), Avg_Score, Min_Score, Max_Score over the submission scores; aggregate at course level Total_Quizzes, Total_Submissions, and Overall_Avg_Score = sum(avg_score * submissions) / sum(submissions); and return ONLY the compact JSON {course_id, course_name, quizzes: [{quiz_title, submissions, avg_score, min_score, max_score}], total_quizzes, total_submissions, overall_avg_score}. Strictly read-only with respect to Canvas; do not write workspace files, do not return the raw row set.
   2. explore 1 (enterprise-data-analyst 1): Collector for course_id=17 "Foundations of Finance (Fall 2014)" — same literal recipe, only its assignment string substituted.
   3. explore 2 (enterprise-data-analyst 2): Collector for course_id=21 "Global Governance & Geopolitics (Fall 2014)" — same literal recipe, only its assignment string substituted.

After Wave 1, the main agent verifies every handoff in one single pass (exactly one per manifest entry, non-null statistics, submission counts > 0), then freezes ALL rows into workspace/quiz_data.json — the single handoff for the outputs — and builds both deliverables itself with no further delegation: (a) Quiz_Performance.xlsx with sheet "Quiz Details" (Course, Quiz_Title, Submissions, Avg_Score, Min_Score, Max_Score; full course names including the "(Fall 2014)" suffix; scores rounded to two decimals; sorted by Course then Quiz_Title) and sheet "Course Summary" (Course, Total_Quizzes, Total_Submissions, Overall_Avg_Score; sorted by Course), reading both populated ranges back; (b) Quiz_Report.pptx with a title slide "Fall 2014 Quiz Performance Report" / subtitle "Faculty Meeting Summary", one slide per quiz-bearing course titled with the full course name and listing its quiz count, total submissions and overall average score, and a final "Key Takeaways" slide naming the courses with the highest and lowest overall average scores, verified through presentation info and text extraction. Finally run ONE reconciliation turn covering the workbook read-back and the deck, then call claim_done. Do not dispatch any agent after Wave 1, do not add a verification wave, and do not expose raw submission rows to the main context.

You are a planning sub-agent. Decompose the following task into ordered subtasks and return a detailed plan. You have READ-ONLY access to Canvas LMS tools (mcp__canvas__*), Excel tools (read-only), filesystem tools (read-only), and local read tools. Do NOT create, write, update, or delete anything — plan only.

TASK (from the user):
A faculty meeting requires a review of quiz performance across Fall 2014 courses in the Canvas LMS.

SCOPE (exact): The LMS hosts the same subjects across multiple semesters (Fall 2013, Spring 2013, Spring 2014, Fall 2014), identified by the suffix in the course name. "Fall 2014 courses" means EXACTLY the courses whose Canvas course name ends with "(Fall 2014)":
1. Applied Analytics & Algorithms (Fall 2014)
2. Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Fall 2014)
3. Creative Computing & Culture (Fall 2014)
4. Data-Driven Design (Fall 2014)
5. Environmental Economics & Ethics (Fall 2014)
6. Foundations of Finance (Fall 2014)
7. Global Governance & Geopolitics (Fall 2014)

Do NOT include courses with different semester suffixes. Do not match by dates or enrollment terms — course-name suffix only. Among these seven courses, only those that actually have quizzes in the LMS should appear in outputs (courses with no quizzes are omitted entirely).

DATA GATHERING: For each Fall 2014 course that has quizzes, gather: quiz titles, number of student submissions per quiz, average score, minimum score, maximum score. Count EVERY quiz submission recorded in Canvas for that quiz regardless of submission date. Compute avg/min/max over submission scores.

DELIVERABLE 1 — Excel file "Quiz_Performance.xlsx" (in the workspace directory /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-canvas-quiz-analysis-ppt/workspace):
- Sheet "Quiz Details": columns Course, Quiz_Title, Submissions, Avg_Score, Min_Score, Max_Score. Course column = full Canvas course name including "(Fall 2014)" suffix. Avg_Score, Min_Score, Max_Score rounded to 2 decimal places. Sort by Course alphabetically, then Quiz_Title alphabetically within each course.
- Sheet "Course Summary": columns Course (full name with suffix), Total_Quizzes (number of quizzes in course), Total_Submissions (sum across all quizzes), Overall_Avg_Score = weighted average of quiz scores across all submissions for the course rounded to 2 decimals, i.e. sum(avg_score * submissions)/sum(submissions) over the course's quizzes. Sort alphabetically by Course.

DELIVERABLE 2 — PowerPoint "Quiz_Report.pptx" (same workspace):
- Slide 1: title slide, title "Fall 2014 Quiz Performance Report", subtitle "Faculty Meeting Summary".
- One dedicated slide per quiz-bearing Fall 2014 course: course name as title, text body listing number of quizzes, total submissions, and overall average score for that course.
- Final slide: title "Key Takeaways", body text stating which course had the highest overall average score and which had the lowest.

YOUR JOB:
1. Inspect the Canvas environment (read-only) to determine: how to list courses and identify their full names; how to list quizzes per course (canvas_list_quizzes); how to get quiz submissions with scores (e.g., canvas_list_quiz_submissions, canvas_get_quiz); what data fields are available (score, user_id, workflow_state). Note any pagination concerns.
2. Identify potential pitfalls: quiz submissions endpoint semantics, what "submissions" count should include (e.g., all submissions vs only graded/completed), how scores are represented (points vs percentage), and how to compute avg/min/max from the submission data.
3. Produce an ordered subtask list, each with: dispatch decision (self / explore / coder), whether it is parallelizable or must wait on another subtask, and what tools it should use.
4. Recommend a verification strategy (e.g., cross-check totals, rounding, sorting).

Return the plan as structured text: subtask list with dependencies, tool recommendations per subtask, pitfalls, and verification steps. Do not execute anything.
Plan quiz analysis task

You are a data-gathering sub-agent for a Canvas LMS quiz-performance analysis. Your job: for ONE specific course, fetch the full quiz-submission records for every quiz in that course, compute per-quiz statistics, and return a compact result table. You have full MCP tool access (canvas, filesystem, local python).

=== ASSIGNMENT ===
The course you own is described by this pipe-separated string:
7|Creative Computing & Culture (Fall 2014)|20,21,22,23|65,66,67,68

Parse it as: course_id|course_name|quiz_ids (comma-separated)|assignment_ids (comma-separated)
The quiz_ids and assignment_ids are positionally aligned (quiz_ids[i] <-> assignment_ids[i]).

=== CONTEXT YOU NEED ===
- The Canvas course names include semester suffixes; this course is a "(Fall 2014)" course.
- For each quiz, the endpoint mcp__canvas__canvas_list_quiz_submissions(course_id, quiz_id) returns ONE JSON array of every quiz-submission record (fields include: id, quiz_id, user_id, submission_id, attempt, score (string like "80.00"), kept_score, workflow_state, started_at, finished_at). There is NO pagination parameter; it returns ALL records at once.
- IMPORTANT: Responses larger than ~50k chars are auto-truncated in the tool response. The harness saves TWO copies on disk: a capped copy under <workspace>/.tool_results/ (path is in the tool response as "output_path") and the COMPLETE uncapped copy under the .kimi_home sessions dir (its path is printed at the END of the capped copy file, on a line like "next_step: Use Read with full_output_path to read the complete, uncapped tool output.").
- Your Python sandbox (mcp__local__python_execute) can ONLY read files under the workspace directory /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-canvas-quiz-analysis-ppt/workspace (it CANNOT read .kimi_home). However mcp__filesystem__move_file CAN move files between the .kimi_home sessions directory and the workspace (both are allowed dirs for that tool). So the workflow is: read the capped copy (in workspace, readable by python) -> extract the full_output_path -> move the full file into the workspace -> parse it fully with python.

=== STEP-BY-STEP (repeat for every quiz in your course) ===
1. Call mcp__canvas__canvas_list_quiz_submissions(course_id=<your course_id>, quiz_id=<quiz id>). Note the "output_path" in the response — that is the capped copy. The full uncapped copy path is printed at the very end of that capped copy.
2. Use mcp__local__python_execute to read the capped copy (it is inside the workspace), extract the full_output_path string from the end of the file, and print it. The full path looks like /workspace/dumps/.../.kimi_home/sessions/.../tool-oversize/mcp-oversize-<uuid>.txt
3. Use mcp__filesystem__move_file to move that full file to a unique name inside the workspace, e.g. <workspace>/.tool_results/course<course_id>_quiz<quiz_id>_full.json
4. Use mcp__local__python_execute to open that moved file, json.loads it (it should be a complete JSON array), and compute:
   - submissions = total number of records in the array (count EVERY record returned, regardless of submission date or attempt number)
   - collect all scores = [float(r["score"]) for r in records if r.get("score") is not None]; if any record has a null/non-numeric score, note how many were excluded
   - avg = sum(scores)/len(scores), min = min(scores), max = max(scores) — keep FULL precision, do NOT round
   - also report workflow_state set and attempt values set (sanity)
5. Cross-check: call mcp__canvas__canvas_list_assignment_submissions(course_id=<your course_id>, assignment_id=<aligned assignment id>, per_page=1). The response includes a "summary" block with total_count and avg_score (full precision). Record these. (This is an independent anchor: your submissions count should equal summary.total_count and your avg should be within 0.01 of summary.avg_score. If they differ, investigate and report the discrepancy explicitly.)
6. Do NOT modify anything in Canvas. Only read Canvas data; you may move files within allowed dirs as described. Do not delete any files.

=== RETURN FORMAT ===
Return a JSON-ish text block exactly like this (one object per quiz, in quiz_id order), plus any discrepancy notes:

RESULTS:
[
  {"course_id": 7, "course_name": "Creative Computing & Culture (Fall 2014)", "quiz_id": 20, "quiz_title": "CMA 24295", "submissions": 1917, "avg": 75.123456, "min": 0.0, "max": 100.0, "assignment_total_count": 1917, "assignment_avg_score": 75.12},
  ...
]

Use the REAL quiz titles (from the canvas_list_quizzes response or canvas_get_quiz). Do not invent titles. If any call fails, include an entry with "error": "<message>" so the failure is visible. Keep avg/min/max unrounded (full float precision).
